source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Scenario planning
finding: Evidence that scenarios help is mostly anecdotal and mostly from Shell. Diffenbach 1983 gives usage, not effect.
numbers: Diffenbach 1983: scenarios were the 3rd most used long-range technique, used by 68% of large organisations surveyed. Shell: 7-9 mini-scenarios cut to 2-3.
quote: There has only been anecdotal evidence offered in support of the value of scenarios
limits: Usage is not effectiveness. Page is tagged as needing citations. Proof said to be unlikely soon because horizons run to decades.
agent_relevance: Do not cite popularity or Shell as proof the scenario step improves answers. Treat as untested design choice (mark [D]).

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Scenario planning, de Geus audit
finding: de Geus's team found the weak link was decision-making after the scenarios, not the scenarios. This is a case claim, not a test.
numbers: No numbers given. Early 1980s Shell audit.
limits: Single firm, internal, not independently checked. Cuts both ways: scenarios may be fine and follow-through weak.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-checked step that forces the agent to act on the chosen scenario set (a decision rule), not just write scenarios.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Scenario planning, criticisms
finding: Listed weaknesses: subjective method, costly, self-defeating forecasts, and assigning probabilities may make people attend only to the likeliest scenario.
numbers: Rule of thumb: about 3 scenarios; more risks overcomplication.
limits: Criticisms are stated, not tested, in the source.
agent_relevance: Do not attach probabilities to the 2-3 scenarios in a way the model then collapses to one; keep them as stress tests.

source: Gokmen & McKiernan (2021) Towards a theory of effective scenario planning: systematic review and critical interpretive synthesis
finding: Systematic review found mostly positive effects on thinking, judgement, decisions, learning and firm performance. Some findings contradicted each other and some showed adverse or no effect.
numbers: Number of studies not stated on the page I opened. No effect sizes.
quote: Some findings were contradictory, with adverse or no effect in some areas
limits: Abstract only (EURAM conference paper). Mix of subjective and objective measures; pooled direction, not size. Effectiveness depends on type, content, information structure and how participants interpret the scenarios.
agent_relevance: Weak, mixed support. Scenario content and framing matter, so test our scenario step against a plain control before adoption.

source: Zanin & Corazza (2021) Scenario planning, strategia e performance
finding: Survey regression: using scenario planning in strategic planning was linked to better firm performance, more so under high environmental change.
numbers: N = 794 Italian SME manufacturers in complex environments. No coefficients on the page.
limits: Cross-sectional self-report survey. Cannot separate cause from firm quality. Full text paywalled; I saw the abstract only.
agent_relevance: Benefit may be conditional on high uncertainty. Use scenarios when the task is open and uncertain, not for closed-form problems.

source: Phelps, Chan & Kapsalis (2001) Does scenario planning affect performance? Two exploratory studies
finding: Two exploratory studies in two industries found better financial performance after scenario planning, with a possible side effect of less focus on customer service. (Seen only in a search-result summary, not opened.)
numbers: No numbers retrieved.
limits: Exploratory, observational, small samples; I could not open the paper (403).
agent_relevance: Oldest quantitative performance test; weak design. Do not rely on it.

source: George, Walker & Monster (2019) Does strategic planning improve organizational performance? meta-analysis (via Wikipedia Strategic planning)
finding: Planning has a positive effect on performance. Benefit depends on formal analysis, comprehensive option generation and stakeholder management, not on having a plan.
numbers: Almost 9,000 organisations. Effect strongest on effectiveness. Effect size not given on the page.
limits: Secondhand via Wikipedia. Scenario planning is not isolated as a moderator. The page has no scenario evidence.
agent_relevance: Closest large-N support: option breadth matters. Maps to our generate-many then cut step, but scenario tools are not tested separately.

source: Hodgkinson & Wright (2002) Confronting strategic inertia in a top management team: learning from failure
finding: A scenario intervention in one top team failed to change strategy because of inertia, politics and non-receptive context. Known as a failure case. (Recalled; not opened.)
numbers: Single-case, no numbers.
limits: One organisation. Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Failure to follow through is the repeat finding (matches de Geus). A lone agent has no politics but can still ignore its own scenarios, so add a check.

source: Healey & Hodgkinson (2008) Toward a pragmatic science of strategic intervention: design propositions for scenario planning
finding: Argues scenario research needs design science with testable propositions, since field evidence is case-based. (Recalled from the title and listing; not opened, publisher returned 403.)
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Frames the gap: no controlled trials of the scenario step. We can run those ourselves on the agent.

source: Kuhn & Sniezek (1996) Confidence and uncertainty in judgmental forecasting: differential effects of scenario presentation
finding: Lab experiment on scenario presentation and forecast confidence; as I recall, scenarios changed confidence without clearly improving accuracy. (Not opened; recollection, check before use.)
numbers: Numbers not retrieved.
limits: Student forecasters; paywalled; my recall of direction is uncertain.
agent_relevance: Warning sign: written scenarios may raise confidence more than accuracy. Needs calibration check in any agent test.

source: Tversky & Kahneman (1983) conjunction fallacy, as summarised in Wikipedia
finding: Adding detail to a story makes it seem more likely though it is logically less likely. This is the core risk of rich scenarios.
numbers: Experts rated Soviet invasion of Poland plus US break in relations at about 4%, versus about 1% for the break alone. Die problem: 65% chose the longer sequence GRGRRR. Linda: 57% still erred with clarified wording. Gigerenzer 1991: frequency format cut errors from about 85% to about 20%.
quote: Experts rated the invasion plus break of relations as more likely than the break alone
limits: Wikipedia summary. Effect shrinks with frequency format, separate evaluation, ability, and consulting others, but is not removed. Persists with real money (Sides 2002).
agent_relevance: Detailed scenarios can inflate their own probability. Rule: judge likelihood on base rates and counts, not on narrative richness.

source: Buehler, Griffin & Ross (1994) planning fallacy, as summarised in Wikipedia
finding: Writing best-case and worst-case scenarios did not fix underestimates: actual time exceeded even the worst-case average.
numbers: N = 37 students. Standard estimate 33.9 days, best case 27.4, worst case 48.6, actual 55.5 days. About 30% finished by predicted time.
limits: Wikipedia summary; small N. Worst-case scenarios were still too optimistic. Outside view helps (not quantified on page).
agent_relevance: Scenario spread is not a calibrated range. Use reference-class base rates to set ranges, then use scenarios as a stress test.

source: Buehler et al. (1995) probability dates, as summarised in Wikipedia
finding: The planning fallacy replicated in confidence-interval form: stated 99% dates were met only 45% of the time.
limits: Student projects, single paradigm.
agent_relevance: Agent stated confidence from scenario-based reasoning should be audited against outcomes.

source: Overconfidence effect, as summarised in Wikipedia
finding: Intervals meant to hold the truth 90% of the time often hit about 50%. Scenario effects and debiasing methods are not covered on that page.
numbers: 90% intervals hit about 50%. 100% certain answers wrong 20% of the time. Oskamp: confidence 33% to 53% as information grew, accuracy under 30%.
limits: Scenario-specific debiasing not covered in this source.
agent_relevance: Baseline: more detail gives more confidence, not more accuracy. Link: Calibration and overconfidence subfield (parallel).

source: Garry, Manning, Loftus & Sherman (1996) imagination inflation, via Wikipedia
finding: Imagining an event raised belief that it happened. Extensions: explaining it (Sharman 2004, 2005) and adding sensory detail (Thomas 2003) gave similar boosts.
numbers: No figures on the page. Pezdek & Eddy (2001) argued regression to the mean; Garry et al. (2001) rebutted.
limits: Memory domain, not forecasting. Transfer to scenarios is by analogy. Contested statistical explanation.
agent_relevance: Writing out a scenario may make it feel real. Cap how much narrative the agent produces per scenario.

source: Halawi, Zhang, Yueh-Han & Steinhardt (2024) Approaching human-level forecasting with language models
finding: A retrieval plus ensemble LM system comes close to the human crowd and beats it in some settings on post-cutoff questions.
numbers: Abstract gives no numbers (Brier scores are in the full text, not read).
limits: Abstract only. Not a scenario method.
agent_relevance: Forecast quality came from retrieval and aggregation, not narrative scenarios. Our scenario step competes with plain aggregation.

source: Schoenegger, Tuminauskaite, Park & Tetlock (2024) Wisdom of the silicon crowd
finding: An ensemble of 12 LLMs matched a human crowd statistically. Showing the human median improved GPT-4 and Claude 2, but plain averaging with humans was better.
numbers: Study 1: 12 LLMs vs 925 humans, 31 binary questions. LLM forecasts sat above 50% though resolutions were near even. Study 2: gains of 17% to 28% with the human median.
limits: Abstract only. 31 questions. Acquiescence bias toward yes.
agent_relevance: Aggregating many samples beats one story. Use ensembling of independent runs rather than one polished scenario.

source: Karger et al. (2024/2025) ForecastBench
finding: On a dynamic benchmark, expert human forecasters beat the best LLM.
numbers: 1,000 questions in the bank; 200-question subset; expert vs top LLM p < 0.001.
limits: Abstract only; margin not on the page.
agent_relevance: LLMs still trail experts on forecasting, so scenario outputs from an LLM need external checking.

source: Rivera et al. (2024) Escalation risks from language models in military and diplomatic decision-making
finding: All 5 off-the-shelf LLMs showed escalation in simulated wargames, with unpredictable patterns, arms races and rare nuclear use.
numbers: 5 models; 10-page body; abstract has no rates.
limits: Simulated wargame, abstract only.
agent_relevance: Scenario-style simulation by LLMs carries model bias; run several models or seeds.

source: Lamparth et al. (2024) Human vs machine: wargame behaviour
finding: LLMs agreed with experts at a high level but differed on individual actions. LLMs were often more aggressive, more sensitive to scenario changes, and ignored player traits. Simulated team talk was poor.
numbers: 214 national security experts; fictional US-China crisis.
limits: Abstract only; no effect sizes on the page.
agent_relevance: LLM stand-ins for stakeholders are unreliable. Do not use persona debate as the check.

source: Elbaum & Panter (2025) Managing escalation in off-the-shelf LLMs
finding: Two simple non-technical interventions substantially cut escalation in the earlier wargame design.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only; interventions not named on the page.
agent_relevance: Prompt-level fixes can shift scenario behaviour; replicate before relying.

source: Zhang, Cao & Liao (2025) XFinBench
finding: Benchmark with scenario planning as one of five capabilities. Best text model o1 scored 67.3% overall and did notably poorly on scenario planning and temporal reasoning.
numbers: 4,235 examples; 18 models; abstract also cites 12.5% for human experts, which looks like a typo.
limits: Abstract only. Scenario planning here means finance problems, not strategy foresight.
agent_relevance: Only benchmark found with a scenario-planning slice; weak model results, but task is not ours.

source: Spaniol & Rowland (2023) AI-assisted scenario generation for strategic planning
finding: Early study of using generative AI to draft scenarios for strategic planning; 83 citations per Crossref. (Page returned 403; contents not read.)
numbers: None retrieved.
limits: Not opened; I do not know its design or results.
agent_relevance: Closest direct LLM-plus-scenario paper found; read before adoption.

source: Crossref listing: LLM and generative-AI scenario papers 2023-2026
finding: Found titles only: GPT-3 exploratory scenario generation (2023), ChatGPT/Bard as red-team avatars for foresight scenarios (2023/2024), ChatGPT for problem-space scenarios (2024), contingency scenario planning with generative AI (2024), LLM risk scenario generation validated against real-world data (2026).
numbers: Citation counts 0 to 4, apart from Spaniol & Rowland at 83.
limits: Titles only; I could not read any of these papers. Mostly exploratory or non-peer-reviewed.
agent_relevance: Gap: I found no controlled LLM study that measures whether scenario steps improve answer accuracy.

source: Search finding: absence of controlled studies
finding: An arXiv search for scenario planning and language models gave 9 hits, none testing a scenario step; scenario planning appeared only as a side task.
numbers: 9 results; two arXiv queries for LLM-scenario plausibility and calibration returned none.
limits: Search coverage limited: Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and the arXiv API were rate limited; WebSearch budget ran out.
agent_relevance: Treat the scenario step as untested for LLMs. Test it in our harness against a plain and a best-of-N control.

source: Chermack & Nimon (2008) effects of scenario planning on decision-making style (via WEF summary in search result)
finding: A study of nearly 90 managers at a US technology firm saw a significant change in decision-making style after scenario planning. (Search snippet only; WEF page returned 403.)
numbers: About 90 managers; no effect size seen.
limits: Single firm, self-report styles; not performance.
agent_relevance: Shows change in style, not better outcomes.
